correctness.rationale: SPD follows from the Schur complement b-k²/a>0. Orthogonal rotation reduces the arbitrary-dimensional star to the coupled matrix [[0,-k/a],[-kt,1-bt]] plus scalar modes. Its characteristic polynomial gives the exact spectral radius and unique minimum at t=1/b. The induced norm is strictly below one iff the explicit 2x2 Gram deficit is positive definite, equivalent to k<a and -k²/a²+2bt-[b²+k²(1-k²/a²)]t²>0; the roots yield the stated exact interval. Symmetry gives equality of worst-case residual and error gains. The explicit SPD family has square of its iteration matrix equal to I/2. Exact rational and seeded numerical checks reproduced the critical identities, but are not the proof.

value.rationale: This is the exact complementary regularization parameter of a recent reduced-basis preconditioner, not an arbitrary family. It supplies a sharp necessary-and-sufficient Euclidean error and residual safety range, compares it with the uniquely fastest spectral parameter, and exhibits an unbounded one-step nonnormality penalty while preserving a fixed asymptotic spectral rate 1/sqrt(2). The intermediate region proves parameter retuning can cure spectral-optimal Euclidean expansion, whereas the third region proves no tuning can cure it. These are structurally informative algorithm-design boundaries; the scope is explicitly restricted to the isotropic-complement family.
